jobs: register the output view modes
turn the worker function into source text
register the workbench components at startup
expose the panel markup on a global
summary: Takes no input and runs once when the file loads. It builds the registry of output views, the source text for the background worker, the component registrations that run when the framework starts, and the global object that holds the panel markup.

jobs: load a script or stylesheet once
skip assets already loaded
summary: Takes the address of a script or stylesheet and resolves when it has loaded, returning at once if that address has already loaded. Rejects with an error naming the address when the browser cannot load it.

jobs: insert a stylesheet or script tag
mark an address loaded when it finishes
summary: Takes the resolve and reject functions for an address, creates a link tag for a stylesheet or a script tag otherwise, and appends it to the document head. It records the address as loaded on success and rejects with a load-failed error naming the address on failure.

jobs: draw a header filter toggle above the table
reserve a note line and a table area
summary: Takes no input and returns the markup for the table view: a strip with a checked checkbox that shows or hides the column header filters, a small note line for row counts, and an empty area where the grid is placed.

jobs: cap the rows shown in the table
write a note when rows are cut
summary: Takes the full row list and returns at most the display limit of rows, writing a note into the table view when the list is longer. The filters see only the shown rows, while copy and download still carry every row.

jobs: refresh table rows in place
decline when the columns have changed
summary: Takes no input and returns true after swapping the rows of the table already on screen for the current data, which keeps its filters and scroll position. Returns false when there is no table, no array data, or the column names differ, which tells the caller to build the table again.

jobs: defer building the table to the next frame
summary: Takes the file being shown and schedules the table build for the next animation frame, so the holding area has been laid out first. Returns nothing.

jobs: build a table grid from the rows
show an error line for bad input
keep the table's column signature for updates
summary: Takes the file being shown and, when the grid library is loaded, builds a grid with one column per key, a filter input in each header, and a height matching its holder. It reads the live data when present and otherwise parses the file text, replaces the holder with an error line if that fails, and records the table and its columns on the holder for later in-place updates.

jobs: show or hide header filter inputs
redraw the grid after a toggle
summary: Takes the change event of the header filter checkbox and shows or hides every filter input in the table holder to match it, then asks the grid to redraw. Returns nothing.

jobs: defer mounting the tree editor to the next frame
summary: Takes the file being shown and schedules the tree editor mount for the next animation frame, so its container is laid out first. Returns nothing.

jobs: load the tree editor on first use
show a read-only tree of the data
show an error line when loading fails
summary: Loads the tree editor module the first time it is needed, then mounts it in the holder using a copy of the live rows when present and otherwise the parsed file text. The tree is read-only, since nothing reads edits back, and the copy means the live rows are never changed through it; an error line replaces the holder if the module or the text fails.

jobs: find a view mode by its id
load the assets a mode needs first
summary: Takes a mode id, loads every asset the mode lists before continuing, and resolves to the mode, or to nothing when no mode has that id. Waits for all of its assets before resolving.

jobs: install the background message handler
collect dollar-prefixed names from source text
summary: Takes no input. It is turned into text and run inside a background worker, where it defines a helper that lists the names a function's source refers to with a dollar prefix and installs the message handler. Because it is turned into text, it cannot reach anything outside itself.

jobs: stack input batches into one list
run chained transform tabs in dependency order
post each tab result as it finishes
report references that never resolve
summary: Takes a message holding the input batches, an optional tag column, the tabs to run, seed outputs, and the names whose output is the input itself. It stacks the batches, tags each row with its batch name when asked, runs the tabs in passes so each waits for the tabs it refers to, and posts each result as it completes. Inputs are copied only while another task still needs the original, and a tab whose reference cannot be met is reported as an error.

jobs: hold a task until its inputs are ready
run one transform task
post its rows or its error back
summary: Takes one pending task and returns true to keep it queued when a tab it refers to is not ready. Otherwise it runs the task over the stacked rows, posts a progress message first and then the rows or the error, keeps the output for a later task that refers to it, and returns false to drop the task from the queue.

jobs: hand over a referenced tab's output
release an output after its last reader
summary: Takes the name of a referenced tab and returns its output for one reader, counting down the readers still to come. It returns a copy while more readers or an alias still need the original, and removes the original from the pool when this is the last reader.

jobs: register the output viewer component
register the workbench component
summary: Takes no input and runs when the framework starts. It does nothing if the framework is missing, and otherwise registers the output viewer component and the workbench component under their names.

jobs: hold the output viewer's state
redraw the view when its mode changes
show one file in a chosen view
summary: Takes an optional options object with a default view and returns the viewer's state and actions. The file, its text and its data are kept on the root element outside reactive state, so the view redraws only when the mode or an explicit revision counter changes, which lets a same-shape data change update a grid in place.

jobs: attach the viewer to its root element
draw the viewer's template in place
summary: Takes no input. It records this viewer on its root element, writes the viewer template into its own element, and once the next render settles, prepares the inner markup for the framework to bind. Returns nothing.

jobs: render the current file in the chosen view
fall back to the first view
summary: Takes no input and returns the markup of the loaded file in the selected view, or an empty string when no file is loaded. An unknown or unset view falls back to the first view in the list.

jobs: store a new file and its data
choose the view to show it in
refresh the table in place when possible
summary: Takes a file name, its text, an optional structured value and an optional wanted view, and keeps them on the root element. It shows the wanted view when the file supports it and otherwise the default, the raw text view, or the first available one. When the table is already on screen and only the rows have changed, it refreshes the table in place; otherwise it switches the view.

jobs: switch the viewer to another view
show a spinner until the view is ready
run the view's after step
summary: Takes a view id and shows a loading spinner, loads that view's assets, then sets the view and bumps the revision so the markup redraws. After the next render it runs the view's after step if it has one and hides the spinner.

jobs: build the workbench's starting state
convert row lists to column form
convert column form back to rows
summary: Takes an optional options object, which can name the storage key for saved tabs, and returns the workbench's starting values with defaults for its input batches, tabs, view and scope selection, pivot settings, dimension pane and bundle fields. It also defines the two helpers that move between a list of rows and a column-wise object, which the export and import paths depend on; the methods that follow are listed as separate units.

jobs: define the dimension pane's scan and tab generators
manage input batches and their references
run tabs through the background worker
load pasted or dropped text as rows
save and restore tabs locally
compress and decompress text
summary: Defines more methods on the workbench state, with no work done at definition time. They cover the dimension pane, input batch intake, renaming and references, the run and per-scope computation through the worker, text intake, saving and restoring tabs, and compression; the short inline ones are accessors for batches and bundle keys, and the longer ones are listed as separate units.

jobs: copy the result or the bundle to the clipboard
toggle the bundle pane open
send rows to the output viewer
switch the visible output view
round a value to set decimal places
summary: Defines more methods on the workbench state, with no work done at definition time. The inline ones copy text with a fallback, toggle the bundle pane, hand rows to the viewer, switch views, round numbers and flash a short confirmation; the rest, including the column profile, the pivot and the layout functions, are listed as separate units.

jobs: set up the clipboard helper once
keep only usable recipes
start with the identity tab
restore saved tabs when persistence is on
summary: Takes no input and runs when the workbench mounts. It creates the shared clipboard helper the first time, keeps only the recipes that have source text, starts with the identity tab alone, restores saved tabs when persistence is enabled, and records itself on its root element.

jobs: take host rows as input
add recipe tabs the host asks for
collapse the editor by default
run the tabs after loading
summary: Takes a row list and an optional metadata object. Rows become a reference batch, an appended batch, or a replacement input depending on the metadata, then any requested recipe tabs not yet present are added. The editor is collapsed unless told otherwise, and the tabs run if there are rows.

jobs: add a recipe as a new tab
focus the tab already using the name
summary: Takes a recipe name. If a tab with that name exists it becomes the active tab; otherwise a new tab is appended from the recipe's source, made active and saved, and the views are refreshed when a run has already happened. An unknown name does nothing.

jobs: add a blank tab
name it with the next free number
summary: Takes no input. It appends an empty tab named with the next unused number, makes it the active tab, and saves the tab list.

jobs: remove a tab by position
keep the last tab and fixed tabs
summary: Takes a tab position. It does nothing when only one tab is left or that tab is fixed; otherwise it removes the tab, keeps the active selection on a valid tab, saves the list, clears the bundle, and refreshes the views if a run has happened.

jobs: switch the active tab
refresh the dimension pane when open
refresh the views after a run
summary: Takes a tab position. It does nothing while a tab name is being edited or when that tab is already active; otherwise it makes the tab active, rescans the dimension pane if it is open, and refreshes the views if a run has happened.

jobs: end an in-place tab edit
save and refresh after an edit
summary: Takes no input. If a tab is being edited, it stops editing, saves the tab list, clears the bundle, and refreshes the views when a run has happened. Otherwise it does nothing.

jobs: describe the active tab's references
count the active tab's rows and columns
summary: Takes no input and returns a short description of the active tab: its name, the tab names it reads, the tab names that read it, and its row and column counts. An unnamed tab is reported as the identity tab.

jobs: select a key candidate's columns in the pick
mark key columns and attribute columns
summary: Takes a candidate entry and replaces the current pick with it: its key columns are marked as keys and its other columns as attributes, and the selection label is set to the key's label.

jobs: save the picked columns as a custom key
rescan and select the new entry
summary: Takes no input. When a key is picked, it stores the key with its picked attribute columns as a custom entry, unless an automatic entry already has that key, then rescans and selects the matching entry. Does nothing when no key is picked.

jobs: remove a custom key entry
rescan the candidates
summary: Takes a candidate entry and deletes the custom definition with the same key label, then rescans. Automatically found entries are not affected.

jobs: group rows by the picked key
count keys that split on each column
build a report and a dimension preview
send the preview to the viewer
summary: Takes no input and works from the picked key and attribute columns on the source tab. It finds how many keys carry more than one combination of attribute values, builds a per-column report and a dimension table where split keys get a numbered suffix and a conflict flag, stores the result, and sends it to the viewer. No tab is created.

jobs: count keys that split on one column
name the worst key for a column
summary: Takes a column name and returns one report row: how many keys hold more than one value for it, its distinct count, the total key count, and the key with the most values along with a few of them.

jobs: add one dimension row per combination
flag rows that come from a split key
summary: Takes one attribute combination and its position among a key's combinations, and appends a dimension row. The first combination keeps the key as it is, later ones get a numbered suffix on the key, and a split key's rows show their position among its combinations in the conflict column.

jobs: send the active preview to the viewer
set the preview banner label
summary: Takes no input. When a preview exists, it sends the report or the dimension rows to the viewer depending on the preview mode and sets the banner label to the preview's label. Does nothing without a preview.

jobs: describe the active tab's references in one line
summary: Takes no input and returns one line listing the tab names the active tab reads and the tab names that read it, separated by a divider. Empty parts are left out.

jobs: count distinct values per column
find the columns each key determines
nest key candidates by what they express
flatten candidates into a display list
summary: Takes no input and scans the active tab's rows up to the scan limit. It finds which columns each candidate key determines, adds the stored custom keys, folds each coarser key under a finer one that can express it, and stores a flat list of candidates with their depth and key count. The rows are not changed.

jobs: find the columns a key set determines
count distinct key combinations
summary: Takes a list of key columns and makes one pass over the scanned rows. It returns the other columns whose value is fixed for every key combination, dropping a column at its first violation, and the number of distinct key combinations.

jobs: flatten a candidate tree into rows
record each candidate's depth
summary: Takes a candidate, its depth, the output list, and a set of candidates already visited. It appends the candidate with its key, columns, key count and depth, then appends its children in order of how many columns each determines, skipping any already visited, and returns the output list.

jobs: make a unique tab name from a seed
summary: Takes a seed value and returns a lowercase name with a dimension prefix built from it, other characters replaced by underscores and cut to thirty characters, with a numeric suffix when a tab already has that name.

jobs: generate source text for a dimension tab
count rows that disagree on their attributes
warn about disagreeing rows when run
summary: Takes a tab name, the key columns and the attribute columns, and returns the source text of a function from rows to rows. The function keeps one row per key, taking attributes from the first row seen; when a key and attributes are both given, it also counts later rows whose attributes disagree and logs a warning with that count when it runs.

jobs: add a dimension tab from a candidate
refresh the fact tab alongside it
summary: Takes a candidate with its key and columns. It appends a new tab whose source is generated from them, marked as waiting for the next run and recording its key and columns, refreshes the fact tab when that option is on, then saves the tab list and clears the bundle.

jobs: add a dimension tab from picked columns
summary: Takes no input. It collects the columns picked as keys and as attributes and, if either set is non-empty, adds a dimension tab from them and clears the pick.

jobs: build the fact tab that drops dimension attributes
reuse the generated fact tab if present
summary: Takes no input. It writes the source of a function that removes every non-key dimension column from the rows, then either rewrites the existing generated fact tab or appends one under a free name. The tab is marked as waiting for the next run.

jobs: save tab names and sources to local storage
skip saving when persistence is off
summary: Takes no input. When persistence is on, it writes the tab names, sources, fixed flags, dimension info and generated flags to local storage, and ignores any storage error. Row data is never written.

jobs: restore saved tabs from local storage
move a value from an older storage key
summary: Takes no input. It moves any value under an older storage key to the current one and removes the old key, then replaces the tabs with the saved list when one exists and makes the first tab active. Storage errors are ignored, leaving the tabs unchanged.

jobs: gzip a text string to base64
summary: Takes a text string and resolves to its gzip compression as base64 text without a data prefix. Uses the browser's built-in compression stream.

jobs: gunzip base64 text back to a string
summary: Takes base64 gzip data of the kind the compressing helper produces and resolves to the original text. The bytes are decoded with the shared decoder before decompression.

jobs: compress selected input batches for export
skip batches already compressed
summary: Takes no input. For each input batch that is selected for the bundle, has rows, and has no compressed copy yet, it stores a gzip of its rows in column form. Returns once all are done.

jobs: flip a bundle key's selection
rebuild the bundle after a change
summary: Takes a bundle key and reverses whether it is included. After a run, it clears the composed bundle and composes it again from the cached compressed parts.

jobs: clear the drop highlight
load a dropped file as text
summary: Takes a drop event and clears the drop highlight. If a file was dropped, it reads its text and passes that to text intake; otherwise it returns nothing.

jobs: restore a workbench from bundle text
decode a compressed paste
load plain text as rows
summary: Takes pasted or dropped text. A bundle with function entries rebuilds the tabs, input batches, selections and dimension info; a compressed string is decompressed and loaded; anything else is loaded as rows. Text that fails any of these steps is loaded as rows.

jobs: rebuild one tab from a bundle entry
restore its output from the bundle data
summary: Takes a function key from a bundle and returns a rebuilt tab with its source text. Its output comes from the combined data entry or, when there is none, from the per-batch data entries; a tab with neither returns nothing.

jobs: parse text as JSON or CSV
turn column data into rows
add pasted rows as a batch or start one
summary: Takes a text string and parses it as JSON, falling back to CSV with a header row. A column-form object is turned into rows. With no batches yet the rows become the first input and run at once with the editor open; otherwise they are added as a batch without running.

jobs: make a batch name unique
summary: Takes an optional base name and returns a name that no existing batch uses, using a default built from the batch count when no base is given and a numeric suffix when the base is taken.

jobs: list the scopes that can be inspected
summary: Takes no input and returns the scopes available to inspect: the combined scope plus each input batch when batches exist, or otherwise the output keys of the first tab that has outputs.

jobs: switch the inspected scope
compute missing outputs for that scope
refresh the dimension pane and views
summary: Takes a scope name and makes it the inspected scope. When rows are loaded and nothing is running, it computes the tabs that have no output for that scope, mirrors the scope onto the tabs, rescans the dimension pane if open, and refreshes the views.

jobs: copy the active scope's output onto each tab
summary: Takes no input. For each tab it copies the output for the active scope into the tab's visible rows, or clears the rows and keeps any error when that scope has no output.

jobs: drop empty rows from pasted data
add rows as a new input batch
summary: Takes a row list, a batch name and optional settings. Rows with only empty values are dropped, the rest become a batch with a unique name, marked as a reference when asked, then the add form closes and the input is refreshed.

jobs: switch a batch between input and reference
summary: Takes a batch position and flips it between input rows and reference data. If the inspected scope was that batch and it became a reference, the scope moves to the combined one, then the input is refreshed.

jobs: finish renaming a batch
run again after a rename
summary: Takes no input. If a batch is being renamed, it stores a safe unique version of the typed name, clears the edit state, refreshes the input and runs again when rows are loaded, since the name is also the tag value.

jobs: rebuild the combined input from batches
mark every tab as waiting for a run
show the input in the viewer
summary: Takes no input. It rebuilds the combined input, sets the scope, and resets every tab to not run while keeping its name, source and fixed flag. It clears the run state and bundle, reports the input to the host when asked, and shows the rows in the viewer.

jobs: run a payload in a background worker
pass progress and results to callbacks
summary: Takes a payload, a result callback and a progress callback. It returns a promise that resolves when the worker reports that it has finished, passing each result and progress message to its callback along the way.

jobs: start a worker from its source text
send the payload to the worker
summary: Takes the promise's resolve function. It builds a worker from the stored source through a temporary object URL, connects its messages, and posts the payload to it. Returns nothing.

jobs: forward progress messages
forward result messages
end the worker when it finishes
summary: Takes a message from the worker. Progress and result messages go to their callbacks; a done message ends the worker, releases its object URL and resolves the promise. Any other message is ignored.

jobs: run the transform tabs
skip when nothing is loaded or a run is active
summary: Takes no input. It does nothing when there are no rows or a run is already going; otherwise it marks the run as going, runs the tabs, and clears the running flag and progress text when done.

jobs: mark stale tabs and every tab that reads them
compute stale tabs for each target scope
rebuild the bundle and refresh the views
summary: Takes no input. It marks as stale each tab that is dirty or has no output for a target scope, plus each tab that reads a stale tab, then computes the stale tabs for every target scope through the worker. Afterwards it clears the bundle, rebuilds it if its pane is open, selects the scope to show, and refreshes the views.

jobs: compute tabs for one scope
pass identity tabs through without the worker
run other tabs in one worker job
summary: Takes a scope name and a list of tab positions. Identity tabs take the scope's input rows directly, while the others run together in one worker job over that scope's batches, with the progress text updated as each finishes. Results are stored on each tab under the scope name.

jobs: compress missing input and output parts
compute any target scope never run
compose the bundle text
summary: Takes no input. If a run has happened and no bundle exists yet, it compresses the input batches it needs, computes any target scope that was never run, compresses each tab's source and column-form output, and then composes the bundle text. It does nothing when a bundle already exists or nothing has run.

jobs: list every possible bundle key in order
summary: Takes no input and returns the ordered plan of bundle keys: one per input batch, then for each tab its source key and its output keys, which are per batch or combined depending on the mode. The bundle writer and its selection list both read this plan so they cannot disagree.

jobs: gather selected compressed parts into the bundle
add a metadata entry for non-default layouts
store the bundle text and its size
summary: Takes no input. It collects the compressed parts selected in the bundle plan into one object, adds a metadata entry that records the combine mode, tag column, batch names and dimension info when the layout is not the plain default, and stores the object as formatted text with its size.

jobs: choose a download or copy payload
pick the format from the view on screen
return the bundle text for the bundle view
summary: Takes a view name and returns the text, file extension and type to copy or download. The bundle view returns the bundle JSON, the pivot and profile views return their own rows, and other views return the active tab's output rows. Raw and tree views give JSON; the table view gives CSV.

jobs: download the bundle as a JSON file
summary: Takes no input. It builds the bundle payload and starts a browser download of it under a fixed file name, releasing the temporary link after a short delay.

jobs: list each bundle key with its selection and size
summary: Takes no input and returns one row per possible bundle key with whether it is selected and the size of its compressed part, blank until that part exists. A metadata row, always selected and fixed, is added when the bundle has metadata.

jobs: show a capped preview of the bundle
say when a run or a build is still needed
summary: Takes no input and returns the text for the bundle pane. It asks for a run first when nothing has run, shows a building note while the bundle is composed, and otherwise shows the first four thousand characters with a count of what is left.

jobs: describe the size of the active view
summary: Takes a view name and returns a short size label: a row count for the pivot, a column count for the profile, and a row count for other views, in thousands when large. Returns an empty string when there is nothing to count.

jobs: render rows as capped JSON text
summary: Takes a row list and returns it as indented JSON for the first five hundred rows, with a note on how many rows were left out when there are more.

jobs: clear any preview
send the active view's content to the viewer
rescan the pivot only when rows changed
summary: Takes no input. It clears any preview, then sends the active tab's rows for the data view, the column profile for the profile view, or redraws the pivot or layout view. The pivot is rescanned only when the rows underneath it have changed, so a dimension toggle keeps the reader's choices.

jobs: profile each column of the rows
summary: Takes a row list and returns one summary per column across all rows: the value types seen, the count of empty values, the distinct count and a sample of sorted values. Distinct counts stop at a cap and are reported with a plus sign past it.

jobs: summarize one column's values
list value types and sample values
summary: Takes a column name and returns its summary across the rows: the types seen, the empty count, the distinct count up to a cap, and up to ten sorted sample values with a count of the rest. Object values are compared by their serialized text.

jobs: read a cell value as a number
accept currency marks and accounting negatives
summary: Takes any cell value and returns it as a finite number, or NaN when it is not one. Strings may carry currency signs, thousands separators, percent signs and spaces, which are dropped without scaling, and parentheses mark a negative value.

jobs: scan the active tab's columns
count distinct values and decimal places
flag columns that are mostly numeric
pick default dimension and measure
summary: Takes no input and reads the active tab's rows. The column list comes from the first five hundred rows, and for each column the counts of distinct values and decimal places cover all rows, with the column flagged as numeric when most filled values read as numbers. It drops selected columns that no longer exist, picks a default row dimension and a measure from its name, uses count as the aggregate when there is no measure, and records the signature of the rows it scanned.

jobs: place a dragged dimension among the row dimensions
summary: Takes a drop position in the row dimension list. It moves the dragged dimension there, or adds it from the pool, takes it out of the column dimensions, and redraws the pivot unless nothing changed. A drop is refused when four row dimensions are already set.

jobs: place a dragged dimension among the column dimensions
summary: Takes a drop position in the column dimension list. It places the dragged dimension there, takes it out of the row dimensions, and redraws the pivot unless nothing changed. A drop is refused when two column dimensions are already set.

jobs: remove a dragged dimension from the pivot
summary: Takes no input. When the dragged dimension is a row or column dimension of the pivot, it removes it from both lists and redraws the pivot; otherwise it does nothing.

jobs: describe the pivot's settings
fall back to counting rows without a measure
summary: Takes no input and returns the pivot's current settings: row dimensions, column dimensions, measure name, aggregate and decimal places. The aggregate is count with zero places when no measure is set, and an average adds two decimal places, capped at six.
